content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple's assistant, and it's now available on iOS 27. I've noticed one standout difference between Siri AI and other AI assistants — and it's the good kind.

The new Siri in iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, and that sets it completely apart from other AI chatbots.

Since the first iOS 27 beta came out, I've been using Siri AI for nearly four months. Overall, Siri AI has met all my expectations.

The new Siri is a huge improvement over the old version, finally delivering on the original promise of a truly capable assistant for Apple devices.

I have to admit that if you need the most cutting-edge, powerful AI tools on the market, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be a better fit for you.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it to those third-party tools, I've found one key difference that makes me prefer Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't ramble, mimic human personalities, or try to build a personal relationship with you.

Siri is practical and smart — it does what you ask it to do. But the way it responds makes it clear that it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you that it's an AI and can make mistakes. It also doesn't pretend to develop any kind of relationship with you.

On the other hand, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are full of personality and subjective opinions, showing a more human-like tendency — but to me, that feels fake.

I know some users enjoy that 'humanised' approach. But I'd rather have an AI assistant that does its job well rather than pretending to be something it isn't.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understands this and has designed the new Siri accordingly.

How 'human-like' do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
